## hotend_fit.cards.snap_lid.SnapLid (class)
SnapLid(opening: 'tuple[float, float]', wall: 'float', *, ctx: 'Any', depth: 'float' = 8.0, name: 'str | None' = None, _shared: 'dict[str, Clearance] | None' = None, _declare: 'bool' = True) -> 'None'
snap_lid: a lid that snaps onto a rectangular opening.

    card = cards.snap_lid(opening=(80, 60), wall=2.0, ctx=ctx)
    box = card.apply_a(box, at=Pos(0, 0, height))    # grooves in the box's inner walls
    lid = card.apply_b(lid, at=Pos(0, 0, height))    # rails under the lid plate

Frame: the origin is the centre of the opening in the plane of the box's rim; +Z points out
of the box; `opening` is the clear inner size along X and Y at the rim.

Half A (the box) needs straight inner walls on the planes x = +/- opening[0] / 2 and
y = +/- opening[1] / 2 from the rim down to `depth`, at least `wall` thick; it gets a short
groove in each of the two long walls. Half B (the lid) needs a plate whose underside is the
rim plane (z = 0); it gets four rails that hang into the opening: two snap rails along the
long walls, each with a bead that rides over the wall and drops into the groove, and two
plain rails along the short walls that locate the lid. The rails are free at their ends so
the snap rails can flex. Pushing the lid on bends each snap rail by the snap undercut; a
rail that is too short for that (too small a `depth`) would break, so the card refuses it
and names the depth that is needed for the material.

Fit pairs, each on both sides: `wall` (snap rail against its wall, slide), `snap` (how far
the bead's crest stands past the wall it rides over; the snap class, negative), `seat` (crest
against the bottom of the groove, snug), `end` (bead end against groove end, loose) and
… [truncated]

## hotend_fit.cards.screw_boss.ScrewBoss (class)
ScrewBoss(screw: 'str' = 'M3', kind: 'str' = 'self_tap', *, height: 'float' = 8.0, plate: 'float' = 2.4, ctx: 'Any', insert: 'str | None' = None, maker: 'str' = 'CNCKitchen', name: 'str | None' = None, _shared: 'dict[str, Clearance] | None' = None, _declare: 'bool' = True) -> 'None'
screw_boss: a boss that takes a screw, and the hole in the part the screw holds down.

    card = cards.screw_boss(screw="M3", kind="self_tap", height=8.0, plate=2.4, ctx=ctx)
    base = card.apply_a(base, at=Pos(x, y, floor + 8.0))   # the boss, standing on the floor
    lid = card.apply_b(lid, at=Pos(x, y, floor + 8.0))     # the screw's through hole

Frame: the origin is the centre of the boss's top face, where the held part rests; +Z points
out of the boss. The boss stands on whatever the host has at z = -height.

`kind="self_tap"`: the screw cuts its own thread in a pilot hole (fit class `thread_tap`).
`screw` is a metric machine screw (`M2` to `M10`) or a tapping screw (`ST2.2` to `ST4.8`).
`kind="heat_set"`: a brass heat-set insert is melted into the boss; the hole is the one the
insert's maker specifies (bd_warehouse table), compensated for this printer.
Half B is a through hole of fit class `thread_free` in a part that is `plate` mm thick there.

The screw and the insert are bought parts: the fit pairs measure the printed holes against
their standard surfaces.

## hotend_fit.cards.peg_hole.PegHole (class)
PegHole(diameter: 'float', length: 'float', fit: 'str' = 'slide', *, ctx: 'Any', through: 'bool' = False, name: 'str | None' = None, _shared: 'dict[str, Clearance] | None' = None, _declare: 'bool' = True) -> 'None'
peg_hole: a round peg on one part and the hole it enters on the other.

    card = cards.peg_hole(diameter=5.0, length=6.0, fit="press", ctx=ctx)
    base = card.apply_a(base, at=Pos(x, y, top_of_base))      # the hole, drilled along -Z
    cover = card.apply_b(cover, at=Pos(x, y, top_of_base))    # the peg, hanging along -Z

Frame: the origin is the centre of the hole's mouth on the face where the two parts meet;
+Z points out of the holed part (A) into the pegged part (B). The hole runs along -Z.

`fit` is `press` (the peg is held by interference), `snug`, `slide` or `loose`. The peg keeps
its nominal diameter as printed and the hole takes the gap. The peg's tip is chamfered and
the hole's mouth is bevelled (0.4 mm at most) so the peg finds its way in, also when the
mouth is the first layer on the print bed. A blind hole is deeper than the
peg by a loose gap along Z so the peg never bottoms out; `through=True` is for a hole that
goes right through part A, which must then be no thicker than `length`.

A press fit drawn with interference overlaps in CAD when the two parts are shown
assembled. That overlap is the joint's own and is allowed for; anything more is reported.
Use the same orientation of `at` for both halves.

## hotend_fit.cards.snap_lid.SnapLid.gauge_dimensions (method)
gauge_dimensions(self) -> 'list[dict]'
What a caliper can measure on this card's printed halves to calibrate the
printer: one entry per dimension with `id`, `half` (the half's name), `feature`
(`hole`: an inside size, which prints small by twice the hole offset; `peg`: an
outside size, which prints large by twice the peg offset), `drawn` (mm, as this
card draws it) and `what` (where to put the caliper, ending with `ABOVE_THE_BED`).
Empty when a card has none.

## hotend_fit.cards.base.Port (class)
Port(name: 'str', location: 'Any', direction: 'tuple[float, float, float]', keep_out: 'Any', note: 'str') -> None
Where a half of the card meets its host part, in the card's frame.

`location` is the port's origin and orientation, `direction` the unit vector along which
the mating half arrives, and `keep_out` a solid (or None), given in the port's own frame
(`location`), that the host must leave empty so the mating half or the bought part has
room. The joint check fails a host that has material there.

## hotend_fit.cards.snap_lid.SnapLid.flex_axes (method)
flex_axes(self) -> 'dict[str, tuple[float, float, float]]'
Per half (`a`, `b`) that carries a part meant to bend (a snap rail): the
direction, in the card's frame, along which that part is long. Printed with this
direction upright the layers lie across the bending part, its weaker direction;
print preparation counts that against an orientation.
